title: Samsung Galaxy S26 256GB for £559.95 on eBay UK: Is It Actually a Good Deal?
content_html:
Deal checked: 16 September 2026. We found a Samsung Galaxy S26 256GB in black on eBay UK for £559.95 from registered business seller Tech Circle. The listing is described as Opened – never used, factory unlocked and carrying 256GB storage with 12GB RAM.

Affiliate notice: Some eBay links in this article are affiliate links. If you buy through one of them, Worth Buying UK may earn a commission at no extra cost to you.

Check the current Samsung Galaxy S26 256GB listing on eBay UK

This one deserves a closer look because the headline saving looks enormous against Samsung's original £879 UK launch price. But there is an important catch: a major UK retailer is currently running Samsung cashback on new Galaxy S26 purchases. Once that is taken into account, the real-world comparison is much closer. That does not make the eBay option poor value; it simply changes what a sensible buyer should compare.

The deal at a glance

  • Product: Samsung Galaxy S26 256GB, black
  • eBay price checked: £559.95
  • Condition: Opened – never used
  • Seller: Tech Circle, registered business seller
  • Seller feedback at time of checking: 100% positive, with more than 4,000 items sold shown on the listing
  • Returns shown on the listing: No returns accepted
  • Charger included: No
  • Network: Unlocked

Is £559.95 genuinely cheap?

Yes, but the fair comparison is not simply £559.95 versus £879.

Samsung launched the 256GB Galaxy S26 in the UK at £879, and Currys was still listing the 256GB model at £879 when we checked on 16 September. However, Currys was also advertising a £250 Samsung cashback offer on eligible Galaxy S26 purchases made between 9 September and 6 October 2026. The cashback is supplied as a virtual prepaid Mastercard through Samsung Wallet and has to be claimed after purchase.

That means an eligible brand-new £879 handset could have an effective post-cashback cost of around £629, assuming the buyer completes the claim successfully and values the prepaid-card reward at its full amount.

Against that more realistic benchmark, the £559.95 eBay listing is around £69 cheaper. That is still a meaningful saving, but it is not the £319 gap suggested by comparing it only with the full retail price.

Why this still qualifies as a Worth Buying deal candidate

The strongest part of the opportunity is that eBay's wider Galaxy S26 marketplace currently contains a cluster of 256GB handsets below conventional retail pricing, rather than one isolated seller claiming an unusually high reference price. When we checked, eBay's Galaxy S26 product page showed multiple Buy It Now options roughly in the £475–£590 range, although condition, seller type, postage, warranty and returns varied substantially.

Compare current Samsung Galaxy S26 256GB listings on eBay UK

That broader market evidence matters. It suggests there is genuine secondary-market price pressure on the S26 rather than a discount that exists only because a seller has chosen an inflated reference price.

What are you giving up for the lower price?

The £559.95 Tech Circle listing is not the same proposition as walking into a major retailer and buying a sealed handset with a straightforward store returns process.

The listing is marked Opened – never used. On eBay, that condition can include items in excellent new condition where packaging has been opened or is no longer sealed. Buyers should therefore read the seller description carefully and confirm exactly what is included before ordering.

The listing also states that no charger is included. That is not unusual for modern flagship phones, but it is worth budgeting for a compatible USB-C charger if you do not already own one.

More importantly, the seller currently states no returns accepted. eBay Money Back Guarantee still applies to most eligible purchases if an item does not arrive or is not as described, but that is different from having a retailer's change-of-mind returns policy. If you simply decide you do not like the phone, the listing terms matter.

Seller check: what we found

Tech Circle is shown as a registered business seller. At the time of checking, the account displayed 100% positive feedback and more than 4,000 items sold. Its detailed seller ratings were also strong, with 4.9/5 for accurate description and 5.0/5 for postage cost, delivery time and communication.

Those signals are positive, but seller history should never replace checking the exact listing. Before paying, confirm the current feedback, seller location, warranty wording, delivery terms and whether the IMEI can be verified as clean and unlocked.

What to check before buying a Galaxy S26 on eBay

1. Confirm the exact model number

For a UK buyer, check that the handset is the UK or otherwise appropriate unlocked model for the networks and features you intend to use. Do not assume that every Galaxy S26 listing is identical simply because the storage and colour match.

2. Ask about warranty status

If the listing says opened, unused or nearly new, confirm whether a Samsung manufacturer warranty remains and when it started. Ask whether proof of original purchase is available if that might be required for a warranty claim.

3. Check the IMEI

For an expensive phone, it is sensible to confirm that the device is not reported lost, stolen or subject to finance problems. A reputable seller should be willing to explain its checks and provide appropriate reassurance without publishing sensitive device information publicly.

4. Read the returns wording

A business seller with strong feedback can still have a listing that says no returns accepted. Understand the difference between a voluntary returns policy and eBay protection if an item is materially not as described.

5. Inspect what is actually included

Check for the original box, USB-C cable, SIM tool and any other accessories you expect. The £559.95 listing specifically states that no charger is included.

6. Compare against current cashback before buying

Samsung promotions can materially change the calculation. A £600 eBay phone may look dramatically cheaper than an £879 retail handset, but a £250 cashback promotion narrows that difference. Always compare the amount you will genuinely end up paying, not just the ticket price.

Who should consider this deal?

This eBay route makes most sense for someone who already knows they want the Galaxy S26, is comfortable buying an opened-but-unused handset, and is prepared to do a few extra checks in exchange for a lower upfront price.

It is particularly attractive if you do not want to wait for cashback, do not want the reward tied to a virtual prepaid card, or simply prefer paying less at checkout.

Who should probably pay more elsewhere?

If you value a conventional returns policy, want a fully sealed retail unit, need a clearly documented manufacturer guarantee, or are uncomfortable checking seller and device details, the extra cost at a major retailer may be worthwhile.

The current Samsung cashback also means buyers should not assume eBay is automatically the best route. A brand-new retail S26 at an effective £629 can be compelling if the extra buyer protections are worth about £69 to you.

Worth Buying verdict

At £559.95, the Tech Circle Galaxy S26 256GB listing qualifies as a strong value candidate rather than an automatic bargain. The price is genuinely below the effective cost of a new £879 handset even after the current £250 Samsung cashback is considered, and the seller history is encouraging. The compromise is the opened condition and the listing's no-returns wording.

For a confident eBay buyer who checks warranty, model details and seller terms first, the saving is meaningful. For anyone who wants the simplest possible after-sales experience, paying more through a participating mainstream retailer may still be the better overall purchase.
